If you specifically want a **blue Staffordshire Bull Terrier (“Staffy”)**, I’d start with breed-club/Kennel Club routes rather than buying from a generic puppy advert. I found a few leads around Scotland, but I’d verify health paperwork and licensing before paying a deposit.

### Places to start

- **[royalkennelclub.com](https://www.royalkennelclub.com/search/find-a-puppy/?ActiveCertifiedBreeder=False&Breeds=Staffordshire+Bull+Terrier&Distance=15&FemaleDogs=False&GeneralRescueClubs=False&HealthTested=False&MaleDogs=False&SearchRescueClubs=False&SortNearest=False&TotalResults=0&utm_source=chatgpt.com)** — its search lets you filter Staffordshire Bull Terriers by location and, importantly, whether the parents have health tests. There are currently blue Staffy litters showing elsewhere in the UK, although I didn't find an Edinburgh litter in the search results. [Royal Kennel Club](https://www.royalkennelclub.com/search/find-a-puppy/?ActiveCertifiedBreeder=False&Breeds=Staffordshire+Bull+Terrier&Distance=15&FemaleDogs=False&GeneralRescueClubs=False&HealthTested=False&MaleDogs=False&SearchRescueClubs=False&SortNearest=False&TotalResults=0&utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- **Luminastaffs, Edinburgh** — a Staffordshire Bull Terrier breeder that says it is based in Edinburgh and raises puppies in the home. I would treat this as a lead to investigate rather than an endorsement: ask for the actual parents' test certificates and details of any current/forthcoming litter. [Luminastaffs](https://www.luminastaffs.co.uk/about-us?utm_source=chatgpt.com) [Luminastaffs](https://www.luminastaffs.co.uk/contact?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- **Caledonred, Edinburgh/Midlothian** — listed as a Staffordshire Bull Terrier breeder with current health tests on Champdogs. [Champdogs](https://www.champdogs.co.uk/breeds/staffordshire-bull-terrier/breeders?ct=Scotland&utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- **Kargonstaffs, West Kilbride** — farther from Edinburgh, but the breeder reports health-tested dogs and membership of both the North of Scotland and Scottish Staffordshire Bull Terrier Clubs. [Champdogs](https://www.champdogs.co.uk/breeder/20826?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- **North of Scotland Staffordshire Bull Terrier Club** — the breed club can be a useful route to established breeders rather than relying solely on classified adverts. The club's puppy-buying guidance specifically stresses DNA and clinical testing. [Staffordshire Bull Terrier Society](https://www.scsbts.com/sbt-welfare-and-rescue/buying-a-puppy/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

There are also current blue Staffy adverts on sites such as Pets4Homes, but I'd use those as **leads rather than proof of a reputable breeder**. [Pets4Homes](https://www.pets4homes.co.uk/sale/puppies/staffordshire-bull-terrier/united-kingdom/scotland/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) 

### What I'd ask the breeder

For a Staffy, these are the big questions:

1. **“Can I see the mother's health-test certificates and the father's too?”**
 The Royal Kennel Club's current Staffordshire Bull Terrier health standard identifies DNA testing for **hereditary cataracts (HC-HSF4-2)** and **L-2-HGA**, plus elbow and eye testing as best practice. [The Kennel Club](https://www.thekennelclub.org.uk/media/cvef530x/kc_health_standard_07-25-web.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
2. **“Has the whole litter had its eyes clinically screened before leaving you?”**
 The Staffordshire Bull Terrier club guidance specifically recommends clinical eye screening of the litter before puppies go to their homes. [Staffordshire Bull Terrier Society](https://www.scsbts.com/sbt-welfare-and-rescue/buying-a-puppy/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
3. **“Can I see the actual test results, rather than just being told the parents are ‘health tested’?”**
 Check the registered names of both parents and independently verify results where possible.
4. **“Can I meet Mum and see where the puppies are being raised?”**
 You should normally see the puppies with their mother in their actual home environment. Be wary if you're offered a car-park handover or asked to meet somewhere unrelated to the breeder's premises.
5. **“Why are you breeding this particular litter?”**
 A good answer should cover temperament, health and suitability for the breed—not simply *“blue puppies are popular.”*
6. **“What health problems have Mum, Dad, siblings and previous puppies had?”**
 Ask for an honest answer, including anything that isn't covered by DNA tests.
7. **“What socialisation have the puppies had?”**
 Ask about household noises, handling, visitors, children, other dogs, grooming, car journeys and being left briefly alone.
8. **“What exactly comes with the puppy?”**
 Ask about microchip, vaccinations, worming, vet examination, KC registration if applicable, insurance, contract, food and after-sales support.

### One important point about “blue”

Don't let the colour be the main selling point. A breeder advertising **“rare blue,” “blue guaranteed,”** or charging a substantial premium purely because of colour isn't, by itself, evidence of good breeding. The Royal Kennel Club's current system explicitly allows puppy buyers to see whether parents meet breed-specific health-testing recommendations, which is much more useful evidence to examine. [The Kennel Club](https://www.thekennelclub.org.uk/media/cvef530x/kc_health_standard_07-25-web.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com) [The Kennel Club](https://www.thekennelclub.org.uk/media/tkzgx4zq/feb-25-kcj-final-online.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com) 

If you tell me **how far you're willing to travel from Edinburgh (e.g. 30, 60 or 100 miles)** and whether you want **a boy or girl**, I can search the current listings and give you a shortlist of blue Staffy breeders/litters to investigate, with the health-testing information for each.
